data.title: SA Asks: What's the best copper stock play right now?
data.description:
Copper prices have been hitting new highs in recent weeks, thanks largely to increased demand due to the AI infrastructure buildout and concerns about potential U.S. tariffs on certain copper products. 

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Andrew Hecht and Zoltan Ban what they thought was the best copper mining stock play right now for investors.

Andrew Hecht: The two purest-play copper mining stocks that move with the metal's price are Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) and Southern Copper (SCCO). 

FCX and SCCO are likely to continue leveraging copper gains, but they may underperform the metal during downside corrections. 

Copper has been in a bullish trend since 2001. It has seen new highs and corrections for years. I view this week's downdraft as nothing out of the ordinary for this volatile market. 

(Andrew Hecht also runs the SA investing group The Hecht Commodity Report.)

Zoltan Ban: First off, I want to emphasize that I am of the view that we are on the cusp of a demand-destruction event as energy prices rise, leading to interest rates rising in correlation due to inflation risk. Copper prices may therefore take a break from the current long-term fundamentals-based rally. 

The AI buildout, as well as the continued rise in EV sales, makes for a strong long-term case for copper prices to continue rising beyond what may be a short-term dip. I have BHP (BHP) on my watchlist for a better buying opportunity. Half of its revenues come from copper. 

I have also been investing in Barrick (B), which is a gold miner, with an eye on the long-term benefits of its rising copper output, particularly as its Pakistan gold-copper project is set to be commissioned and start ramping up output in the next few years. The Reko Diq project is currently on hold due to security issues in the area; however, it carries great potential, especially if one believes in the long-term fundamentals driving the copper market.

If I am correct and copper prices will dip in the next few months as energy prices and interest rates continue to rise, it may be a good buying opportunity.

data.title: Wall Street climbs after the latest inflation report comes in largely in line
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages pushed higher Friday after the latest consumer inflation report came in largely in line with expectations.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last +1.1%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last +1%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last +1.2%. 

From a sector-by-sector vantage point, all of the 11 segments were up in the green, with communication services leading the charge. At the other end of the spectrum, health care has been the weakest performer. 

U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in August, matching forecasts after a 0.1% gain in July and leaving the year-over-year rate unchanged at 3.4%. Core CPI (ex-food and energy) increased 0.3% versus the 0.2% consensus and prior reading, while the annual core rate eased to 2.4% from 2.5%, in line with estimates. 

“Friday's CPI print was in-line with expectations, but inflation is still too hot, and the Federal Reserve's hands are tied. A rate hike next week is all but assured. Consumer prices are going in the wrong direction, and remain significantly higher than the Fed's 2% target,” Skyler Weinand of Regan Capital stated. 

U.S. Treasury yields were mixed. The U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield (US2Y) moved up 4 basis point to 4.63%, the U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield (US10Y) was lower by 1 basis point to 4.95%, and the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield (US30Y) dipped 2 basis points to 5.34%. 

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of Dell Technologies (DELL) climbed higher by +10.2%, while shares of Albemarle Corporation (ALB) fell -2.9%

data.title: UBS: Two Fed hikes are coming — Bonds still belong
data.description:
UBS expects the Federal Reserve to raise its policy rate by 25 basis points on September 16 and to deliver another quarter-point increase in December.

That trajectory would shrink the current yield advantage short-duration bonds enjoy over cash. Even so, the bank still sees a case for keeping bonds in portfolios and for spreading income sources more widely.

Investors should look past the very shortest maturities when seeking diversification. As the Fed moves onto a hiking path, the potential for capital gains in ultra-short bonds is likely to fade. Those same securities, however, continue to generate healthy income at today’s elevated yields. Yield and rate expectations are evolving, yet bonds remain a core source of portfolio income.

UBS anticipates that returns will be driven mainly by the high level of starting yields now on offer. That cushion should help the asset class absorb further volatility.

In short, the coming rate increases change the relative appeal of cash versus short bonds, but they do not eliminate the role of fixed income as an income engine or a source of resilience.

data.title: Tesla unveils European Semi specs
data.description:
Ahead of its official launch at the IAA Transportation show in Hannover, Germany, Tesla Europe (TSLA) published the specifications for its European Semi electric truck.

The electric truck will have a range of up to 550 km (342 miles) at 40 tonnes fully loaded on an 822 kWh battery. This compares to a range of 850 km (500 miles) for the American version with a full load of 37.2 tonnes (the shorter range could be attributed to the higher weight).

The European version is also lighter with a curb weight of ~20K lbs versus ~23K lbs for the U.S. Semi.

Tesla Europe (TSLA) did not specify what the Semi will cost, nor when it expects to deliver the truck to customers.

Electrek also pointed out other issues European drivers might have with the Semi, namely the shorter range than its U.S. counterpart and a longer charging time. The European version can recover ~60% of range in 30 minutes with a megacharger at up to 800 kW, while in the U.S., the Tesla Semi charges at 1.2 MW, recovering 70% in 30 minutes.

data.title: NewFortress Energy completes restructuring; trading halted
data.description:
Trading is halted on New Fortress Energy (NFE) after the company said Friday it completed its restructuring plan that lowers its debt to $700M from $5.7B.

As a result of the completion, New Fortress' (NFE) Brazilian business and operations have been separated to establish two distinct, standalone enterprises: BrazilCo and "New NFE."

The company said ​the transaction extinguished ~$5.7B of third-party debt with creditors receiving all the equity of BrazilCo, preferred equity of New NFE with $2.45B of liquidation preference, 65% of the common equity of New NFE, and $571.3M of New NFE term loans; New ​NFE also raised $136.5M in new financing.

"The UK RP restructuring results in the New NFE being a much simpler, more streamlined company," New Fortress (NFE) CEO Wes Edens said. "The company owns a portfolio of critical LNG and power assets, including a substantial and growing LNG portfolio, terminal operations and logistics in Mexico and Puerto Rico and a 735 MW power and turbine portfolio. These assets and operations produce significant cash flow today and when fully deployed in the coming months provide the opportunity for significant growth."

data.title: Axsome rises on Auvelity prescription data
data.description:
• Axsome Therapeutics (AXSM) is up ~6% in Friday trading following data showing that prescriptions for Auvelity (dextromethorphan and bupropion) reached a record high.
  • Data from Symphony Health, part of HealthVerity, found that scripts for the depression and Alzheimer's disease agitation treatment reached hit ~23,500 this week. 
  • The US FDA granted the Alzheimer's agitation indication in late April. 
  • Mizuho analyst Graig Suvannavejh, who rates Axsome at outperform, said that "while still early days in the launch, this appears highly indicative of a strong start for Auvelity in ADA."

data.title: Butler National outlines scalable aerospace growth with record $51.1M backlog while extending DraftKings deal through 2030
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Butler National Corporation (BUKS) Q1 fiscal 2027

Management View

  • Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) framed the quarter as operationally strong, saying, "It has been another successful quarter for Butler National" and "the business continued to perform exceptionally well," while reporting year-over-year gains in profitability and revenue mix led by aerospace.
  • Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) reported the segment driver and profitability profile, including, "Total revenue for the quarter was $30.8 million compared to $20.1 million in Q1 fiscal '26, up 53%" and "our overall operating margin increasing to 24% compared to 23% in the prior year quarter."
  • Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) highlighted aerospace scale and demand visibility, stating, "Aerospace Products segment revenue was $21.7 million compared to $11.3 million in Q1 fiscal '26, a 92% increase" and "our Aerospace Products backlog reached a record $51.1 million at July 31, '26."
  • Jeffrey Yowell (Executive Chairman) emphasized Avcon’s shift toward intellectual property and higher-value solutions, explaining, "STCs create intellectual property, kits allow us to scale that intellectual property and mission systems integration allows us to provide a higher value, more comprehensive solution to the customer."

Outlook

  • Management did not provide formal forward guidance ranges for revenue, EPS, or margins in this transcript; Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) cautioned on variability, saying, "I do want to be careful about suggesting that either business will grow at the same rate every quarter or every year" and "investors should not assume that any individual quarter represents a permanent margin level."
  • On aerospace growth capacity and margin trajectory, Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) said, "An important part of our strategy is growing areas of the business that will allow us to leverage our engineering and certification expertise without requiring a proportional increase in physical labor and capacity," adding, "Kit sales are a good example."
  • On long-term pro services stability despite economics changing, Jeffrey Yowell (Executive Chairman) described the contract extensions as providing "long-term stability and visibility for an important component of our professional services business," while noting, "we agreed to a lower revenue participation percentage than under the original agreement."

Financial Results

  • Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) reported profitability and per-share results, stating, "Net income for the quarter was $5.3 million" and "Earnings per share for the quarter was $0.08."
  • Aerospace performance was concentrated in Aircraft Modifications, with Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) reporting, "the Aircraft Modifications division had an exceptional 189% increase in revenue to $16.3 million," and adding that Aerospace Products "maintain[ed] an operating margin of approximately 25%."
  • Professional Services showed mixed drivers, as Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) said, "traditional casino gaming revenue increased to $6.8 million" while "Mobile sports wagering revenue decreased slightly to $1.1 million," attributing the decline to "a decrease in the hold percentage during the quarter."
  • Liquidity and leverage moved favorably, with Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) stating, "We ended the quarter with $35.3 million of cash and cash equivalents," alongside, "Stockholders' equity increased 5% during the quarter, while total liabilities decreased 11%."

Q&A

  • Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) read a growth-sustainability question on Avcon and Tempe, and responded, "We remain very positive about the long-term opportunities" but noted results can vary because "the timing of aircraft deliveries, customer orders, government programs and certification activities can create variability in our results."
  • Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) asked Jeffrey Yowell (Executive Chairman) to detail Avcon’s model; Yowell answered, "Developing an STC requires expertise in engineering, certification work, investment and time," and added, "If we can engineer and certify a modification and then manufacture a kit that can be shipped to qualified installation partners, we can potentially sell that solution repeatedly."
  • Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) asked about rebranding KC Machine; Jeffrey Yowell (Executive Chairman) said, "The change from KC Machine to Butler Machine is more than simply a name change," positioning it toward "complex, higher-value manufacturing opportunities in aerospace, defense and other mission-critical markets."
  • Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) addressed backlog definition and conversion, stating, "backlog represents contracted business" but "does not necessarily occur on a straight-line basis," and added, "we maintain a pipeline of future potential opportunities that we are actively pursuing."
  • Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) covered capital allocation, saying, "Our first priority is investing in our existing business" while also noting, "we continue to evaluate -- capital allocation strategy when we believe repurchasing shares represents an attractive use of shareholder capital," and "we remain open to inorganic growth opportunities."
  • Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) asked about Boot Hill sports wagering; Jeffrey Yowell (Executive Chairman) said the Kansas Lottery extension "extends our management of sports wagering operations through 2030" and the DraftKings amendment was extended "for 10 years," while acknowledging, "the economics of the DraftKings agreement are less favorable."
  • Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) asked about the permanent CEO search; Jeffrey Yowell (Executive Chairman) said the Board is "actively evaluating a number of external candidates" and "the process may take some time," adding, "Our priority is finding the right person rather than establishing an artificial deadline."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst sentiment was not observable because the operator stated, "today's call will not include the live Q&A session," and the Q&A consisted of pre-submitted questions read by management.
  • Management sentiment was confident but cautious on variability, with Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) saying, "We remain very positive about the long-term opportunities" while warning, "investors should not assume that any individual quarter represents a permanent margin level."
  • Versus the prior quarter, management’s tone remained continuity-focused on strategy and leadership transition; Jeffrey Yowell (Executive Chairman) reiterated a similar framing, saying in Q1 FY27, "our objective is finding the right leader," following Q4 FY26: "shareholders should view this as a leadership transition, not a change in strategy."

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Aerospace visibility increased, with Q1 FY27 backlog described as "a record $51.1 million," compared with Q4 FY26: "our backlog is a record high at $47.1 million."
  • Professional Services narrative shifted from local economic pressure to contract durability and economics; in Q4 FY26 Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO & President, CFO) cited "economic challenges in the local market," while in Q1 FY27 Jeffrey Yowell (Executive Chairman) focused on extensions that provide "long-term stability" but at "a lower revenue participation percentage."
  • Leadership-transition messaging stayed consistent; Q1 FY27 emphasized, "we're comfortable" with the CEO search taking time, while Q4 FY26 emphasized, "The vetting process will not be trivial" and "not simply move quickly."

Risks and Concerns

  • Margin and revenue timing risk was tied to program cadence; Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) said, "The timing of aircraft deliveries, customer orders, government programs and certification activities can create variability" and that backlog conversion depends on "regulatory approvals, material availability" and other factors.
  • Sports wagering economics reset was explicitly acknowledged; Jeffrey Yowell (Executive Chairman) said, "we agreed to a lower revenue participation percentage," even as the extensions provide longer-term operating continuity.
  • Capacity constraints were described as multi-factor; Adam Sefchick (Interim CEO, President & CFO) said, "There isn't one capacity constraint that applies to every project," citing potential pacing items including "engineering resources" and "hangar availability."

Final Takeaway

Management described Q1 fiscal 2027 as a quarter of sharp aerospace-led growth and higher profitability, highlighted by record aerospace backlog visibility and a deliberate push to scale Avcon through STCs, kit programs, and mission systems integration. In Professional Services, management emphasized long-term sports wagering stability through extensions with the Kansas Lottery and DraftKings while acknowledging less favorable revenue participation terms, alongside continued Board-led work to hire a permanent CEO without changing strategy.

data.title: Spider-Man’s box-office reign could get tangled up by ‘Practical Magic 2’
data.description:
Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) is looking to take the top spot at the North American box office this weekend with “Practical Magic 2,” as the Warner Bros. (WBD) sequel opens against Sony Group’s (SONY) “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which has led the domestic chart for six consecutive weekends.

Forecasts for the Sandra Bullock-Nicole Kidman sequel vary. Boxoffice Pro projects a $40 million-$50 million opening, while Variety expects $30 million-$40 million from about 4,000 North American theaters. The trade publication expects “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” to take in $9 million to $11 million in its seventh weekend, while Universal’s (CMCSA) "The Odyssey" is projected at $6 million to $8 million.

The “Practical Magic” sequel is being released by Warner Bros. (WBD) at a time when the major-studio release calendar has been relatively light, giving the film a chance to capture demand after a record-setting summer for US theaters. Boxoffice Pro described it as the week’s destination movie by default amid the shortage of major studio releases.

For “Spider-Man,” the weekend could mark another milestone even as it loses the top spot. The Sony-Marvel film is closing in on the domestic box-office record held by “Star Wars: The Force Awakens,” which finished its run with about $936.7 million. Current tracking expects “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” to surpass that mark this weekend, ending the more than decade-long reign of “The Force Awakens.”

The weekend follows a record US summer box office of about $4.76 billion, underscoring the strong momentum heading into the fall release slate.

data.title: Pharming wins approval of Joenja for younger age group
data.description:
• The US FDA has approved Pharming Group's (PHAR) Joenja (leniolisib) for children between the ages of four and 11 with a kind of rare genetic immune system disorder.
  • The treatment was previously approved in 2023 for individuals 12 years and older with activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta syndrome (APDS).
  • Approval was based on safety and pharmacokinetic data from a single-arm, open-label study.
  • Individuals with APDS suffer from recurrent infections, especially in the sinuses, ears, and respiratory tract. They also develop enlarged lymph nodes, tonsils, and spleen.
